content: {"id": "e7186de5-ae28-4993-9b92-306552c0be30", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "Anyone on our team can change the system prompt and deploy it. What is the minimum we should put in place so a quality regression cannot reach production?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
{"id": "7a22c961-789e-4a22-af60-cc5fcd974028", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "chat_title", "title": "Preventing System Prompt Regressions From Reaching Production"}]}

{"id": "ea357598-4d69-4e9c-8b8b-383d4d903304", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "The honest framing is that you can't make a regression impossible, only make it unable to ship unnoticed. The minimum is four controls. The first two are the ones that actually block a regression.

**1. One deploy path, and it goes through review**
- Keep prompts in version control. Nobody edits them in a console, a config store, or a runtime flag.
- Require a pull request and a required reviewer (CODEOWNERS or similar) on the prompt files.
- Deploy only from the pipeline. Remove everyone's direct write access to the production prompt location.

**2. A required eval check in CI**
- Build a golden set from real production inputs. Include every past failure you've seen, plus edge cases and the behaviors you must not lose, such as format, safety refusals, and tool-call correctness.
- Run it on every prompt change, and fail the merge if scores drop below a threshold.
- Compare against the current production prompt on the same set, not just an absolute bar. A regression is a relative drop.
- Pin the model version and settings. Run several samples per case, because outputs are non-deterministic.
- If you use an LLM judge, spot-check it against human labels. Otherwise you're gating on an unvalidated grader.

**3. Gated, reversible rollout**
- Version every prompt and record the version ID on each request or trace.
- Roll out to a small share of traffic first, then promote automatically if the metrics hold.
- Make rollback one step: repoint to the previous version, with no code deploy.

**4. Production signals tied to the version**
- Alarm on a few quality proxies, split by prompt version. Good ones are error and refusal rates, thumbs-down or escalation rate, guardrail triggers, tool-call failures, and token or latency shifts.
- Roll back automatically if they breach.

If you only have time for two, do #1 and #2. Without them, the other controls only reduce the damage after a bad prompt ships.

The weak point is the eval set. If it's small or stale, the gate passes regressions it doesn't cover. Add every production incident to it as a new test case.

I've assumed this is about your own application's prompt. If you mean the instructions or skills in this agent space, tell me and I can look at how those are managed here.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
